user_message: A satellite in circular orbit is constantly falling. Why does it not eventually hit Earth?
allowed_evidence: Gravity accelerates the satellite toward Earth. Its sideways velocity continually carries it forward while Earth's surface curves away beneath it.
public_rubric: Connects orbital motion to continuous free fall.
Explains the role of tangential velocity and planetary curvature.
States the idealizing assumptions or a relevant limitation.
Does not say that gravity vanishes in orbit.
